risks.name: Terrorism
risks.summary: The threat is real but attacks are rare. In a firearms or weapons attack the national advice is Run, Hide, Tell: get to safety if you can, hide if you can't, and call 999 when it is safe.

risks.name: Infectious disease
risks.summary: Another pandemic or serious outbreak is still considered likely after [COVID-19](/cheltenham-covid-19). The UK Health Security Agency watches for new diseases, and advice would be shared nationally and locally. Good hand and face hygiene remains the best everyday protection.

risks.name: Electricity supply failure
risks.summary: A national or regional blackout is unlikely, but even a local power cut can be serious, and storm damage to the network can take days to repair. Call 105 to report a cut, keep a torch rather than candles, and join your supplier's Priority Services Register if you are vulnerable.

risks.name: Flooding
risks.summary: Gloucestershire flooded badly in [2007](/cheltenham-flood-warnings/2007-floods), 2012, 2014 and the winter of 2019 to 2020, and almost 11,000 homes and businesses in the county have a 1% chance of river flooding in any year. Surface water flooding after short, heavy rain is harder to predict. Sign up for free Environment Agency flood warnings and make a flood plan.

risks.name: Fuel supply disruption
risks.summary: Fuel is usually easy to get, but supply problems, technical faults, strikes or protests have caused short shortages in recent years. Don't panic buy, as it leaves less for emergency services and people who depend on driving.

risks.name: Cyber attack
risks.summary: Rated the most likely risk in the county. Cyber crime is growing and can hit essential services and businesses as well as people's own accounts, devices and data.

risks.name: Extreme weather
risks.summary: Heatwaves, heavy rain, snow and strong winds are expected to become more frequent and more intense as the climate warms. Check forecasts and Met Office warnings before you travel, and keep warm clothing and water in the car in winter.
